correctness.rationale: The cap-triangle identity is exact whenever every side receives a sample; independent monotone-chain shoelace constructions checked 3,635 such configurations. The complementary event is exponentially rare, with a uniform deterministic bound on both area loss and the capped corner sum. The two-neighborhood binomial void probability integrates explicitly to a factor P²/((N+1)(N+2)) times four endpoint-power terms, giving the asserted exponentially accurate mean for each fixed polygon. Joint endpoint gap survival functions converge to independent unit exponentials, with uniform exponential marginal tail bounds proving moment convergence at every fixed order. The exact Laplace transform follows by conditioning on one unit exponential. Finite simulations of triangle, pentagon and heptagon mean and variance agree within declared statistical tolerances; no universal step relies on simulation. The domain excludes successive collinearity and zero sides.

originality.rationale: The NEW non-entailed claim is the finite-sample rational mean law with exponentially small edge-length corrections for any fixed convex polygon, not the already-known local Poisson process convergence. The 2023 boundary-polytope volume theorem states a power law with unspecified constant; its published theorem and area proof do not supply all algebraic corrections or a sharp exponentially small remainder. The 2024 polygon Hausdorff theorem establishes joint local Poisson convergence, so the weighted-product limit is acknowledged as a mathematical consequence of older process theory after inserting the exact corner-area identity, not credited as independent discovery. A public Gumbel finding concerns a maximum of Hausdorff errors, not the finite-N mean formula. Searches showed no published-finding corpus item giving the same mean identity; failure of search is not proof of absolute novelty. Historical priority remains qualified.

value.rationale: The problem is the natural metric of how much area a convex polygon loses when replaced by the hull of boundary samples, studied in earlier geometric approximation literature. A single exact perimeter–angle coefficient controls its finite-N expected deficit up to exponentially small error, so there are no side-length-sensitive algebraic corrections. This non-asymptotic structure goes well beyond generic orders and gives practical benchmarks for stochastic approximation; the acknowledged weighted-product corollary exposes the relevant non-Gaussian uncertainty and a complete Laplace transform. The theorem applies to all fixed polygons with genuine corners, not an arbitrary isolated parameter choice.
